Reviewed sync/async blocking, cancellation, timeout, pagination, streaming/backpressure, duplicate delivery, indeterminate commit, transaction mismatch, credentials, injection, versioning, migration, aircraft, payment, and intensive-care cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter requires rejection or target-contract change whenever the adaptee cannot satisfy a stronger required property.

proof_review.notes: Physical calibration, sensor accuracy, concurrency, network, timestamp validity, and clinical/avionics safety remain outside the proof.

evidence: Audited compatible, equivalent, exact, lossless, valid, refinement, round trip, atomic, async, durable, proof, and safety language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Round-trip claims have domains and observational equivalence; proposed expert and operational evidence is not described as completed.

Network, concurrency, fuzz, differential, protocol, device, calibration, avionics, and clinical evidence remain future requirements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production compatibility, physical accuracy, external practitioner, academic, aviation, or clinical review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes structural from semantic adaptation, defines partial/lossy/refining mappings, and integrates units, identity, time, errors, asynchronous effects, transactions, security, and migration.

practitioner_review.notes: The guidance supplies mapping inventories, explicit target errors, bounded blocking bridges, pagination/backpressure contracts, contract/property/fuzz/differential tests, safe diagnostics, version support, and adapter retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter builds from a formal target/adaptee relation through practical boundary dimensions, provides a runnable exact conversion, ten diverse examples, and five exercises with complete design and high-stakes answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
